Growth Infrastructure Company

Find and Fix the Growth Leaks Costing Your Business Revenue

Soto Growth Systems is a growth infrastructure company for established, owner-led businesses. We diagnose the ten Growth Leaks™ silently draining leads, follow-up, and sales capacity — then design and install the systems that close them.

Quick answer: A growth infrastructure company builds and repairs the operating systems behind your marketing — lead capture, speed-to-lead, follow-up, sales process, CRM discipline, KPI visibility, and accountability — so the leads you already generate are captured, answered, followed up, and tracked instead of lost. Soto Growth Systems diagnoses these systems, designs the fix, and can install it for you.

Take the Free Growth Leak Score See the 10 Growth Leaks

Free, self-serve, about five minutes. No login required.

The Pattern We See

Your business generates leads. It just doesn't convert them consistently.

Most owner-led companies we meet are not short on demand. They have a market, a reputation, and a pipeline of inbound interest. What they don't have is a reliable system for turning that interest into booked, closed, repeatable revenue.

Leads sit unanswered for hours. Follow-up depends on whichever team member remembers to do it. The CRM has fields nobody fills in. The owner still has to check on deals personally to know if anything is moving. None of this shows up as a single dramatic failure — it shows up as revenue that should have closed and didn't, quietly, every week.

These are Growth Leaks: specific, identifiable breakdowns in how a lead moves from first contact to closed customer. Each one is fixable on its own. Left alone, they compound — a slow response makes follow-up less likely to land, weak follow-up makes the sales process inconsistent, and an inconsistent sales process makes it harder for the owner to step back from day-to-day deals.

The owner usually senses that something is off long before anyone can name it. Revenue is unpredictable month to month. Good months don't repeat reliably. The team is busy, but busy doesn't always mean productive in the pipeline. Naming the specific leak is the first step toward fixing it instead of just working harder around it.

Why Marketing Alone Doesn't Solve This

More leads won't fix a leaky growth system.

The default response to inconsistent growth is to spend more on marketing. More ads, more content, more lead sources. If the system receiving those leads is leaking — slow response, weak follow-up, no sales process, no visibility into what's actually happening — additional volume just increases the size of the loss.

A growth infrastructure company works upstream of marketing spend. Before adding volume, we look at what happens to the leads you already have: how fast they're contacted, how consistently they're followed up with, whether your sales process is repeatable, whether your CRM data can be trusted, and whether anyone besides the owner is accountable for the outcome.

Marketing fulfillment — websites, SEO, advertising, content, reputation — has its place, and our partner network handles that work. Soto Growth Systems owns the layer underneath it: the operating system that determines whether marketing dollars convert into revenue at all.

The Diagnostic Framework

The 10 Growth Leaks™

Every owner-led business we've assessed loses revenue somewhere across these ten points. Most have several active at once.

01

Lead Source

Lead sources are unclear, untracked, or over-concentrated in one channel.

02

Lead Capture

Inquiries arrive through forms, calls, or messages that aren't consistently logged anywhere.

03

Speed-to-Lead

New leads sit for hours before anyone reaches out.

04

Follow-Up

Follow-up happens once, or not at all, instead of on a defined cadence.

05

Appointments

Scheduled calls and estimates are missed, rescheduled, or never confirmed.

06

Sales Process

Every rep, or the owner, sells a different way with no repeatable structure.

07

CRM Discipline

The CRM exists but the data in it can't be trusted or acted on.

08

KPI Visibility

No one can say, without guessing, what's actually happening in the pipeline this week.

09

Accountability

No one owns follow-through on leads, tasks, or deals once they're assigned.

10

Owner Bottleneck

Growth stalls whenever the owner isn't personally involved in every deal.

Get your Growth Leak Score™ in about five minutes

Quick answer: The Growth Leak Score™ is a free, self-serve diagnostic. Answer 10 questions, and in about five minutes you get an instant score out of 100, right in your browser. Fractional Growth Operator™

Fractional Growth Operator: The Ongoing Operating Layer for Your Growth System

A Fractional Growth Operator keeps your Growth OS running after it is built — reviewing KPIs, pipeline health, follow-up discipline, CRM adoption, and accountability on a fixed cadence, so the system doesn't quietly decay once the implementation team moves on.

Quick answer: A Fractional Growth Operator is the ongoing operating layer included in Growth OS Managed Implementation™ and available as a standalone engagement after any completed implementation. It is not a starting point and not a fourth peer offer on the value ladder — it is what keeps a built system operating correctly over time. It starts at $5,500 per month with a 6-month minimum and no setup fee. Scope and cadence are confirmed on a strategy call or at the close of an implementation phase.

Take the Free Growth Leak Score Compare Implementation Options

What a Fractional Growth Operator Actually Is

A Fractional Growth Operator is not a marketing hire, a virtual assistant, or a project manager. The role exists to operate the Growth Operating System that Soto Growth Systems designs and installs — keeping pipeline discipline, follow-up execution, CRM data quality, KPI reporting, and accountability rhythms intact after the building phase ends.

Most owner-led businesses do not fail at building a system. They fail at operating it consistently once the initial energy of an implementation fades. Fields stop getting filled in. Follow-up sequences get skipped when someone is busy. KPI dashboards go unreviewed for weeks. The Fractional Growth Operator function exists specifically to prevent that decay by keeping a fixed, recurring review rhythm in place.

This is why the role is positioned where it is: inside Growth OS Managed Implementation™, and as a standalone continuation after any completed implementation — Growth OS Blueprint™, Growth OS Guided Implementation™, or Managed. It is never sold as a first step, because there is nothing to operate until a Growth OS has been designed and installed.

Not a Fourth Peer Offer, Not a Starting Point

This distinction matters enough to state plainly, twice.

What it is

  • The operating layer built into Growth OS Managed Implementation™
  • A standalone continuation available after any completed implementation phase
  • A recurring cadence of review, reporting, and accountability
  • Scoped only once a Growth OS already exists to operate

What it is not

  • Not a fourth tier alongside Blueprint, Guided, and Managed
  • Not an entry point for businesses without an existing Growth OS
  • Not a marketing execution or ad-spend management service
  • Not a substitute for sales closing, hiring, or legal/accounting decisions

The Operating Cadence

The Fractional Growth Operator function runs on a fixed, recurring rhythm rather than ad hoc check-ins. The exact frequency — weekly or biweekly — is confirmed in scope before the engagement starts.

  1. Weekly or biweekly Growth OS review

    A structured check of the system as a whole: pipeline movement, follow-up execution, CRM data discipline, and any Growth Leak that has reopened since the last review.

  2. KPI review

    The metrics defined during implementation are reviewed against the KPI dashboard installed for the business — not new metrics invented after the fact.

  3. Growth Leak monitoring

    Each of the 10 Growth Leaks™ is monitored for early signs of regression: a lead source going quiet, response times slipping, CRM fields going unfilled, or accountability slipping in one part of the team.

  4. Monthly executive reporting

    A monthly report to ownership on what is working, what has drifted, what needs a decision, and what is scheduled next. This is a status and accountability report, not a performance guarantee.

  5. Quarterly strategic planning

    A quarterly session to reassess priorities, confirm the operating rhythm still fits the business, and decide whether scope should expand, hold, or wind down.

Why Diagnosis Comes First

Most growth problems in owner-led businesses aren't a single broken tool — they're a chain of small failures across lead source, lead capture, speed-to-lead, follow-up, appointments, sales process, CRM discipline, KPI visibility, accountability, and owner bottleneck. Buying implementation before diagnosis means paying to build the wrong thing, in the wrong order, on top of a process no one has mapped.

Before any implementation work begins — whether you do it yourself or SGS does it for you — the business needs an honest picture of which leaks exist, why they exist, and which one to fix first. That picture is what a diagnosis produces. It's also what separates a Growth Operating System from a pile of disconnected fixes.

Why a Blueprint Comes Before Implementation

Skipping the blueprint and jumping straight to CRM configuration or automation is how businesses end up with tools that don't match their sales process, pipelines that don't reflect reality, and dashboards no one trusts. The blueprint is what makes Guided Implementation and Managed Implementation faster and more accurate — the design work is already done before a single workflow gets built.     You have a capable operations lead or owner with the time to run the plan, your team can absorb CRM and automation work internally, and you're comfortable executing a written roadmap without weekly outside oversight.

  2. Choose Guided Implementation if...

    You have some internal capacity but want SGS managing the project, sharing accountability for deadlines, and building the CRM and workflows alongside your team rather than handing you a plan to execute alone.

  3. Choose Managed Implementation if...

The three implementation options are not separate products. They are one Growth Operating System delivered at increasing levels of hands-on support.

A documented Growth OS, a configured CRM, and a trained team are necessary — but none of it produces anything if the system isn't used consistently. Adoption is the difference between a Growth Operating System and an expensive tool that gets ignored after week three.

This is why Guided and Managed Implementation both include weekly or biweekly review rhythms, KPI visibility, and accountability installation rather than a one-time build-and-leave engagement. It's also why Self-Implementation includes an executive workshop and training sessions rather than just a written report — a plan no one internalizes is a plan no one follows. At the Managed level, adoption monitoring continues through the Fractional Growth Operator™ layer specifically because systems degrade without an outside party checking usage, not because the initial build was flawed.

Soto Growth Systems cannot guarantee that a business adopts its own system. What SGS controls — and commits to — is a defined implementation process, documented deliverables, agreed quality checks, and transparent reporting on what's been completed, what remains open, and what the client must do next.

Starting investments above assume a single-location business with standard complexity. The following factors increase price at any level because they increase the actual work required:

Why Start Free

Why the Free Growth Leak Score Is the Right First Step

The Growth Leak Score™ is a free, self-serve, 10-question diagnostic. It gives you an instant score out of 100 and a top-3 priority repair sequence based on your answers — no commitment, no cost, and no obligation to buy anything.

Business results depend on market conditions, lead volume, offer quality, team adoption, sales execution, pricing, and other factors outside SGS's control.

FAQ

Implementation Options: Frequently Asked Questions

What are the growth systems implementation options at Soto Growth Systems?

Soto Growth Systems offers three implementation options after diagnosis: Self-Implementation (Growth OS Blueprint™, starting at $7,500 one-time), Guided Implementation (starting at $18,000 + $4,500/month), and Managed Implementation (starting at $35,000 + $8,500/month). Each delivers the same Growth Operating System design at a different level of hands-on support.

Yes. Every implementation option assumes a completed Growth Leak Score™ or Professional Growth Leak Assessment™. Implementation without diagnosis means building against a guess instead of documented findings.

Yes. The Growth OS Blueprint™ is built for self-implementation. SGS diagnoses, designs, documents, and teaches; your team executes the roadmap, SOPs, and training. It does not include CRM configuration, automation building, or hands-on technical work.

What if my team doesn't have time to implement the Blueprint ourselves?

You can move to Guided Implementation, where SGS manages the project and builds the CRM and workflows alongside your team, or Managed Implementation, where SGS owns the entire build. Work already completed under the Blueprint carries forward and isn't repeated.

How is Guided Implementation different from Managed Implementation?

Guided Implementation is done-with-you: SGS and your team build the system together, and your business must provide an internal implementation owner, access, and team attendance. Managed Implementation is done-for-you: SGS owns the full build, configuration, training, and stabilization, and continues with ongoing Fractional Growth Operator™ support.

What is a Fractional Growth Operator™?

The Fractional Growth Operator™ is the ongoing operating layer included in Managed Implementation and available standalone after any implementation. It provides regular Growth OS review, KPI review, Growth Leak monitoring, a monthly executive report, and quarterly strategic planning.

What increases the price above the starting investment?

The timeline pauses rather than the scope expanding. Guided Implementation requires an internal implementation owner, system access, team attendance, and timely approvals to stay on schedule.

Is Managed Implementation a fully hands-off engagement?

No engagement is fully hands-off. Even under Managed Implementation, the client retains business decisions, legal and compliance approval, pricing decisions, hiring decisions, timely access, accurate information, and final approval of customer-facing messaging.

The Growth OS Blueprint™ (Self-Implementation) is delivered in 4–6 weeks. Guided Implementation has a 3-month minimum, with a defined 90-day sequence. Managed Implementation has a 6-month minimum, with implementation typically running 90–120 days followed by stabilization.

A connected system for turning opportunity into consistent execution

A Growth Operating System connects the people, processes, tools, measurements, and accountability required to create and convert opportunities.

It is not simply a CRM, marketing plan, dashboard, or collection of software tools. It is the operating structure that helps the business consistently move from strategy to execution.

SGS uses the Soto Growth OS framework to identify where the system is breaking down and determine what should be repaired first.

The system connects:

  • Speed-to-lead and follow-up
  • Appointments and sales execution
  • CRM and pipeline discipline
  • KPIs and performance visibility
  • Accountability and ownership
  • Automation and repeatable execution
  • Owner independence and scalability

03

Acceleration

Expand what is working through optimization, automation, and accountability.

  • Continuous optimization

How SGS applies the framework
